title: Microsoft argues coding benchmarks cannot choose the best model for your stack
friendlyTitle: The top coding model on a leaderboard may not be best for your team
summary: Microsoft’s developer guidance explains why public coding scores may not predict performance on proprietary frameworks, team conventions, instruction files or tool-heavy agent environments. It recommends using public benchmarks as a capability filter, then testing representative tasks inside the actual harness and codebase.
friendlySummary: Public tests use popular open-source projects and simple setups. Your code, rules and tools are different, so a high score may not lead to better results at work.
whyItMatters: Model selection should be treated as an internal evaluation problem, not a leaderboard purchase decision. A small, repeatable suite of real team tasks can reveal regressions, context failures and total task cost that public scores miss.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Use leaderboards to make a shortlist. Then test each model on real tasks from your own codebase before choosing one.
